scope: NUCLEO-WB55RG application flash 0x08000000..0x0807FFFF recovery identity followed, only after dual backup admission, by the existing production-off SSD1681 0x2F/0x2D diagnostic

help_relevant_verbatim: -u,     --upload       : Upload the device memory content to a .bin/.hex/.srec/.s19 file
<address>          : Start address of read and upload
<size>             : Size of memory content to be read

PROVEN: The preceding Goal permanently records that the lower-driver agent overwrote the retained host E1997F... build artifact and made zero hardware contacts afterward.
The preceding candidate HEX remains byte-identical at SHA-256 52D79C... and its diagnostic is default-disabled, production-off, and independent of normal panel initialization.
The locally installed official STM32CubeProgrammer v2.22.0 help defines SWD HOTPLUG as a connection mode and -u/--upload as device-memory export to a file.
The active WB55 linker script assigns exactly 512K of application FLASH beginning at 0x08000000; 0x80000 bytes ends at 0x0807FFFF.
Two 524288-byte uploads can be compared byte-for-byte and screened for all-zero/all-FF content and a plausible Cortex-M vector table before any write is admitted.
The prior runner already orders serial readiness before candidate flash and avoids a post-flash reset, but its old normal-HEX restore contract must be replaced rather than weakened.
INFERENCE: Because the preceding programmer-verified restore installed E1997F... and this work has made no later hardware contact, the current board is expected to still contain those prior application bytes.
If two independent HOTPLUG uploads are identical and pass length/content/vector checks, their shared raw SHA-256 is adequate as a new pre-run application-byte identity for one bounded restore cycle.
A post-restore HOTPLUG upload equal to backup-a proves restoration to the captured pre-run application bytes, not reproduction of the lost E199 Intel HEX file or its file hash.
UNKNOWN: The board application raw SHA-256 and vector words remain unknown until the two admitted uploads complete.

HOTPLUG's exact transient electrical/runtime effect on this connected MCU is not proven to be absolutely zero; the defensible boundary is zero write, erase, reset, halt, run, read-unprotect or option-byte command before backup admission.
SSD1681 chip status, 0x2D display option bytes, VCOM, F6 ping-pong state and waveform version remain unread.
The board contents are not currently available as a reusable host artifact and must not be called an E199 HEX reconstruction.
RISK: Any accidental reset, erase, write or read-unprotect before two valid backups would destroy the only recoverable pre-run application identity.
A short, long, inconsistent, all-zero/all-FF or implausible-vector upload may be transport failure or protected/invalid content and must terminate without retry or write.

After candidate programming is attempted, failure to perform the single restore or failure of post-restore byte comparison leaves the board in an uncertain application state and requires immediate human escalation without a second write.
Starting the serial capture after flashing would miss the sole diagnostic boot; resetting after serial open would execute the read groups twice.

ADMISSION.backup_pass: two independent 524288-byte nontrivial files, byte-identical and SHA-identical, valid MSP/reset vector
ADMISSION.candidate_write_admission: all non-hardware gates and dual-backup gate PASS
ADMISSION.restore: at most one backup-a write after any candidate write attempt, programmer verify, then one HOTPLUG upload and byte/hash equality
ADMISSION.future_only: A later Goal may consider read-only 0x41/0x27 around one official partial update; this Goal does not read RAM or refresh the panel.

non_goals: Recreate or claim the lost E199 Intel HEX file hash
Read above 0x0807FFFF, option bytes, secrets, controller RAM, 0x41 or 0x27
Read-unprotect, tune LUT/OTP/0x37/0x20, refresh the panel, or perform visual/White/Black/rail/temperature/animation work
Claim zero residue, OLED-like behavior, production readiness, T03 binding or temperature-complete CWF1
